text:
Calm yourself, my grief, and make your anguish serene.

You longed for night. It is descending. Here it is.
A dark atmosphere covers Paris, bringing
peace to some and sorrow to many others.
While the crowd that yields to Pleasure,
its relentless executioner, roams the streets
hunting remorse beneath the wakeful feast,
you, grief, come to me. Give me your hand as you see
how it is possible to escape the already dead years
in their old garments upon heaven’s balcony.
Disillusionments now rise, as from the sea,
when the sun beneath an arch dies in the distance.
Now, like a shroud descending from the east.
Observe, my grief: the immense night advances.

translation.title: Recollection
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the supplied Spanish version credited in the source to José Emilio Pacheco. The catalog title is blank; the English title is translated transparently from the explicit body heading ‘Recogimiento.’ A malformed soft-hyphen sequence is silently normalized.
